cases.question: How high must the lowest floor of a new house be built in the floodplain?
cases.answer: New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure must have the lowest floor elevated to at least one foot above the base flood elevation. After construction is complete the permit holder submits an Elevation Certificate documenting the as built elevation of the lowest floor.

cases.question: Do I need a permit before developing land in a special flood hazard area?
cases.answer: A floodplain development permit must be obtained before any development begins within an area of special flood hazard. The requirement applies to all areas of special flood hazard in the unincorporated portions of Harris County.

cases.question: What must a floodplain development permit application include?
cases.answer: The application is made on the form supplied by the county and includes a site plan drawn to scale, the proposed elevation of the lowest floor of all structures, and a description of the extent to which a watercourse will be altered. Where elevation data is required the application also carries the certification of a registered professional engineer or licensed surveyor.

cases.question: Can I place fill in the regulatory floodway to level out my lot?
cases.answer: Encroachments within the adopted regulatory floodway are prohibited, and fill is named as an encroachment. The only exception is where a registered professional engineer certifies through hydrologic and hydraulic analysis that the proposed encroachment will result in no increase in flood levels during the base flood discharge.

cases.question: If I remodel my house and the repairs cost more than half its value, do the flood rules apply to the whole house?
cases.answer: Work of that scale is a substantial improvement, which the regulations define as any repair, reconstruction, or improvement whose cost equals or exceeds fifty percent of the market value of the structure before the improvement begins. A substantially improved structure is held to the same standards as new construction.

cases.question: Is there any way to get an exception to the flood elevation requirements for a historic building?
cases.answer: A variance may be issued for the reconstruction or rehabilitation of a structure listed on a register of historic places, provided the work does not preclude the structure's continued designation as a historic structure. A variance otherwise requires good and sufficient cause and a determination of exceptional hardship.

cases.question: What are the penalties for building in the floodplain without getting a permit first?
cases.answer: Developing land in an area of special flood hazard without first obtaining a floodplain development permit is an offense, and each day a violation continues is a separate offense. Civil penalties reach five thousand dollars per calendar day under the Texas Water Code chapter cited in the ordinance. The county may also seek an order to remove the unpermitted work.

cases.question: Who decides whether my land is inside the 100-year flood zone?
cases.answer: The Harris County Engineer serves as the Floodplain Administrator and determines whether a parcel lies within the one hundred year flood zone by interpreting the adopted Flood Insurance Rate Map. That determination governs unless the Federal Emergency Management Agency amends it.

cases.question: Do I have to prove my finished floor height after construction is complete, or only before?
cases.answer: Both. A certificate based on construction drawings or on a building under construction is provisional, and upon completion of construction a new certificate based on finished construction must be submitted so the as built elevation of the lowest floor is on record. The certificate is prepared by a licensed surveyor, engineer, or architect.

cases.question: Who is allowed to sign and seal Section C of the Elevation Certificate?
cases.answer: Section C must be completed by a land surveyor, engineer, or architect authorized by law to certify elevation information in the state where the building is located, and that professional must sign, seal, and date the certificate. A property owner, builder, or insurance agent may not certify Section C.

cases.question: When should an applicant use Form MT-EZ instead of the full MT-1 application?
cases.answer: Use MT-EZ for a simple Letter of Map Amendment request covering a single structure or a single parcel of legally recorded land on the basis of natural high ground. Use the full MT-1 package instead when the request involves fill, multiple structures, multiple lots, or a Letter of Map Revision.

cases.question: Do manufactured homes have different flood elevation rules than regular houses?
cases.answer: Manufactured homes are held to the same elevation standard and to an additional one. They must be elevated on a permanent foundation so the lowest floor is at or above the required elevation, and they must also be securely anchored to resist flotation and lateral movement.

cases.question: What happens if my project changes after the floodplain permit was approved?
cases.answer: The permit holder submits a revised site plan and revised elevation data and obtains an amended permit before continuing work. Work performed outside the scope of the approved permit is treated as unpermitted development.

cases.question: Is a drainage study required for site development in the floodplain?
cases.answer: Yes. Site development within an area of special flood hazard must be supported by a drainage study showing that the proposed grading and detention will not increase runoff onto adjacent property, and the study must be sealed by a registered professional engineer.
